description: The mathematics of better decisions: linear and integer programming, network flows, decision analysis, queueing and simulation. Students formulate real problems, solve them by hand and with solvers, and interpret the answers for managers.
modelledOn: Hillier and Lieberman, Introduction to Operations Research
Winston, Operations Research: Applications and Algorithms
outcomes: Formulate a word problem as a linear or integer programme with clear variables, objective and constraints.
Solve linear programmes graphically and with the simplex method, and interpret dual values and sensitivity ranges.
Model and solve transportation, assignment, shortest path, maximum flow and project network problems.
Analyse decisions under risk and uncertainty with decision trees, expected value, information value and utility.
Predict waiting-line performance and evaluate systems by Monte Carlo and discrete-event simulation, then present a recommendation.

units.title: Modelling and linear programming formulation
topics: What operations research is: models, decision variables, objective, constraints and the modelling cycle
Formulating linear programmes: product mix, diet, blending and transport problems
Graphical solution in two variables: feasible region and corner points
Standard and slack forms; basic feasible solutions
LP assumptions: proportionality, additivity, divisibility and certainty

units.title: The simplex method and solvers
topics: Simplex tableau and pivoting: entering and leaving variables, ratio test
Degeneracy, cycling and Bland's rule; detecting unbounded and infeasible problems
Artificial variables: the two-phase method and Big-M
Revised simplex, computational complexity and an overview of interior-point methods
Solving with software: SciPy and PuLP models, reading solver status and output

units.title: Duality and sensitivity analysis
topics: Primal-dual relationship; weak and strong duality
Complementary slackness and the dual simplex method
Shadow prices and reduced costs as economic quantities
Sensitivity ranging of objective coefficients and right-hand sides
Changes after optimality: adding a constraint or a new variable

units.title: Network models
topics: Transportation problem: northwest corner, least cost and Vogel starting methods; MODI optimality test
Assignment problem and the Hungarian method
Shortest paths: Dijkstra's algorithm, Bellman-Ford and the LP view
Maximum flow and minimum cut: Ford-Fulkerson and the max-flow min-cut theorem
Minimum-cost flow and minimum spanning trees
Project networks: CPM and PERT as optimisation models

units.title: Integer programming
topics: Integer, binary and mixed formulations: knapsack, facility location and scheduling
LP relaxation and why rounding fails
Branch and bound: bounding, pruning and search strategies
Cutting planes: Gomory cuts and branch and cut
Logical conditions with binary variables and big-M constraints

units.title: Decision analysis
topics: Decisions under uncertainty: maximin, maximax, Hurwicz and minimax regret
Expected monetary value and decision trees with rollback
Expected value of perfect and sample information; Bayes' revision
Utility theory and risk attitudes; building a utility curve
Multi-criteria decisions: weighted scoring and the analytic hierarchy process
Goal programming and Pareto efficiency

units.title: Queueing, simulation and inventory
topics: Queueing structure: arrival and service processes and Kendall notation
M/M/1 and M/M/c steady-state measures; Little's law
Finite queues and M/G/1 with the Pollaczek-Khinchine formula
Monte Carlo simulation: pseudo-random numbers and inverse-transform sampling
Discrete-event simulation: event list, clock advance and output analysis with confidence intervals
Inventory models: economic order quantity, reorder point and the newsvendor problem

units.title: Modelling case studies with solvers
topics: Case: staff rostering and timetabling for a clinic or school
Case: moving produce from farms to markets as a transport and vehicle-routing problem
Case: staffing a bank or mobile-money agent point using queueing and simulation
Validation, verification and communicating model results to managers
Project: build, solve and defend a model of a local problem

schedule.title: Formulating linear programmes
schedule.exercise: Formulate four word problems as linear programmes (including a cocoa-processing product mix) and solve the two-variable one graphically.

tasks.title: Plot the constraints of a two-variable product mix, shade the feasible region, and find the best corner point by evaluating the objective
Formulate a diet problem with five foods and four nutrient constraints and check the model by testing a hand-picked feasible plan
Examine a case where a stated LP model breaks proportionality or divisibility, and decide how to repair or replace the model with justification

schedule.title: The simplex method
schedule.exercise: Solve a three-variable maximisation by the simplex method by hand and then a minimisation using Big-M, recording every tableau.

tasks.title: Step through the simplex tableau for a two-constraint problem, choosing the entering and leaving variables at each pivot
Solve a minimisation with greater-than constraints using the two-phase method and verify that the final objective matches the graphical result
Construct a degenerate LP, show a cycling risk with a naive rule and resolve it with Bland's rule in the tableau

schedule.title: Solvers and implementation
schedule.exercise: Code a blending model in Python with a solver library, then extend it with a new constraint and report how the plan changes.

tasks.title: Solve a product mix LP with a solver library and print the objective, variable values and the solver status
Model a 20-variable feed blending problem in code, generate the data from a table and explain which constraints are binding
Implement a basic revised simplex on a small LP and compare iteration counts and run time with a library solver on random instances

schedule.title: Duality and sensitivity
schedule.exercise: Write the dual of a production LP, read shadow prices from the solver, and advise a manager whether to buy more of a scarce resource.

tasks.title: Write the dual of a given primal LP and confirm that both optimal objective values agree using a solver
Compute allowable ranges for each objective coefficient and right-hand side of a solved LP and state when the optimal basis changes
Add a new product and a new constraint to a solved LP, test by reduced cost and dual feasibility whether re-solving is needed, and verify

schedule.title: Transportation and assignment
schedule.exercise: Plan the shipment of fertiliser from three depots to five markets and assign six drivers to six routes at least cost.

tasks.title: Find a starting plan for a 3 by 4 transportation problem with the least-cost and Vogel methods and compare the two costs
Solve a 5 by 5 assignment problem with the Hungarian method, showing each reduction and covering step
Model a transport network as an LP and as Dijkstra, find shortest routes between two towns and explain why the answers agree

schedule.title: Flows, spanning trees and project networks
schedule.exercise: Find the maximum flow and minimum cut of a water distribution network and compute the critical path of a clinic construction project.

tasks.title: Step through Ford-Fulkerson on a small network, recording augmenting paths until no path remains, then name the minimum cut
Build a minimum spanning tree for a village power network with Kruskal and Prim and compare the total cable length
Draw a 15-activity project network, compute the critical path and crash it to meet a deadline at minimum added cost

schedule.title: Integer programming
schedule.exercise: Choose which of eight clinic sites to open under a budget with a binary model, and solve it by branch and bound.

tasks.title: Step through branch and bound on a small knapsack, recording the bound at each node and which branches are pruned and why
Solve a facility location model with binary variables in code and compare the result with rounding the LP relaxation
Model a fixed-charge problem and either-or constraints with big-M, then test how the choice of M affects solve time and solution validity

schedule.title: Decisions under uncertainty and risk
schedule.exercise: Evaluate a farmer's decision to plant a drought-resistant crop using a decision tree, then compute what a perfect forecast is worth.

tasks.title: Apply maximin, maximax, Hurwicz and minimax regret to one payoff table and compare the four recommended actions
Draw a decision tree with chance and decision nodes for an equipment purchase and roll it back to the expected monetary value
Compute the expected value of sample information from a test with given accuracy using Bayes' revision and decide whether it is worth its price

schedule.title: Utility and multi-criteria decisions
schedule.exercise: Build a utility curve for a risk-averse decision maker and rank four site options with a weighted scoring model and the analytic hierarchy process.

tasks.title: Plot a utility curve from three lottery questions and classify the decision maker as risk averse, neutral or seeking
Compute analytic hierarchy process weights from a pairwise comparison matrix, check the consistency ratio and rank the alternatives
Formulate a two-objective problem as goal programming, trace the Pareto frontier by varying weights and plot the trade-off

schedule.title: Queueing models
schedule.exercise: Dimension the number of tellers for a branch with given arrival and service rates so the average wait stays below four minutes.

tasks.title: Compute utilisation, average queue length and waiting time for an M/M/1 queue and check Little's law on the results
Find the smallest number of servers in an M/M/c queue that keeps the probability of waiting below 20 percent
Simulate an M/G/1 queue with high service-time variance and compare the measured waiting time with the Pollaczek-Khinchine prediction

schedule.title: Simulation and inventory
schedule.exercise: Simulate a day at a fuel station with random arrivals and compare policies, then set the order quantity for a pharmacy item.

tasks.title: Estimate pi and an expected profit by Monte Carlo with 1,000 and 100,000 samples and compare the errors
Write a discrete-event simulation of a single-server queue and report mean wait with a 95 percent confidence interval over 30 runs
Find the newsvendor order quantity for uncertain demand analytically and by simulation and explain any difference in the two answers

schedule.title: Case studies: rostering, routing and service points
schedule.exercise: Model one of three cases from raw data to a recommendation: clinic roster, farm-to-market distribution or a mobile-money agent point.

tasks.title: Solve a small nurse rostering model with coverage and rest constraints and check the resulting roster by hand
Model produce transport from three farms to four markets as a transportation problem with capacity limits and read the shadow prices
Use simulation to compare one fast agent against two slow agents at a busy mobile-money point and recommend a staffing plan

schedule.title: Validation and project defence
schedule.exercise: Present a model of a local problem to a mock manager panel, with validation evidence, sensitivity analysis and a clear recommendation.

tasks.title: Review a model report in a case and list its validation gaps, such as untested assumptions and missing data checks
Build and validate the project model against historical data, reporting where model output and observed values disagree
Run sensitivity and scenario analysis on the project model and recommend a decision, stating which assumptions would change the answer
